payload.text: For the selected reading can we import book cover images via this method? Open Library Covers API Our Covers API provides a programmatic method to access the book covers and author photos available in the Open Library Covers Repository. Guidelines for Cover Use Please, do not crawl our cover API. If you do, we may decide to block your crawl. Our covers are available for download in bulk on archive.org (example), but, it's a bit of a jungle in there, and is updated regularly. If you want to display covers on public-facing pages, please use a src URL that points to covers.openlibrary.org. For example, if you'd like to call a cover using an ISBN, you can do it like this: A courtesy link back to Open Library is appreciated, whether it be on each individual book's page (where you can link back to the book's page on Open Library, for example, using the same ISBN https://openlibrary.org/isbn/9780385533225), or on your About page or in your footer. Thanks! How To Book covers can be accessed using Cover ID (internal cover ID), OLID (Open Library ID), ISBN, OCLC, and LCCN. The covers are available in 3 sizes: S: Small, suitable for use as a thumbnail on a lists section of a work on Open Library, M: Medium, suitable for display on a details page on Open Library and, L: Large The URL pattern to access book covers is: https://covers.openlibrary.org/b/$key/$value-$size.jpg Where: key can be any one of ISBN, OCLC, LCCN, OLID and ID (case-insensitive) value is the value of the chosen key size can be one of S, M and L for small, medium and large respectively. By default it returns a blank image if the cover cannot be found. If you append ?default=false to the end of the URL, then it returns a 404 instead. The following example returns small sized cover image for book with ISBN 0385472579. https://covers.openlibrary.org/b/isbn/0385472579-S.jpg The same cover can be accessed in multiple ways using different keys: https://covers.openlibrary.org/b/id/240727-S.jpg https://covers.openlibrary.org/b/olid/OL7440033M-S.jpg https://covers.openlibrary.org/b/isbn/0385472579-S.jpg https://covers.openlibrary.org/b/isbn/9780385472579-S.jpg https://covers.openlibrary.org/b/lccn/93005405-S.jpg https://covers.openlibrary.org/b/oclc/28419896-S.jpg Author Photos Author photos can be accessed using OLID and ID. The URL Pattern for accessing author photos is: https://covers.openlibrary.org/a/$key/$value-$size.jpg For example the following is the photograph of Donald E. Knuth from the Open Library. https://covers.openlibrary.org/a/olid/OL229501A-S.jpg Cover Size & API Access You can add .json to end end of cover urls to return API information about the cover, e.g. https://covers.openlibrary.org/b/id/12547191.json. One can fetch the image off-screen and use it's width/height: async function fetchImage(url) { const img = new Image(); return new Promise((res, rej) => { img.onload = () => res(img); img.onerror = e => rej(e); img.src = url; }); } const img = await fetchImage('https://covers.openlibrary.org/b/id/12547191-L.jpg'); const w = img.width; const h = img.height; This one way one won't need to make two separate requests per image! The browser won't make a second request for the image if you set the src of your visible element after fetching it in this way. Rate Limiting The cover access by ids other than CoverID and OLID are rate-limited. Currently only 100 requests/IP are allowed for every 5 minutes. If any IP tries to access more that the allowed limit, the service will return "403 Forbidden" status. Bulk Access The covers API is intended for displaying covers on public facing websites and not for bulk download. If you are interested to download the covers in bulk, please download them from: Small Covers: https://www.archive.org/details/s_covers_0000 ... https://www.archive.org/details/s_covers_0006 Medium Covers: https://www.archive.org/details/m_covers_0000 ... https://www.archive.org/details/m_covers_0006 Large Covers: https://www.archive.org/details/l_covers_0000 ... https://www.archive.org/details/l_covers_0006 Original Covers: https://www.archive.org/details/covers_0000 ... https://www.archive.org/details/covers_0005 Each of these archive.org items have 100 tar files, each containing 10K images in each. The names of these files are based on the cover ids. For example, s_covers_0005_32.tar file contains images for CoverIDs from 5320000 to 5329999. The mapping from various IDs to CoverIDs is available at: https://www.archive.org/download/ol_dump_2011-03-31/ol_dump_coverids_2011-03-31.txt.gz It has 4 columns ID-Name, ID-Value, OL-KEY and CoverID.

# AI Reading List: Library Annotations and ISBNs

**Essential literature for understanding artificial intelligence** spans technical foundations, critical perspectives, industry narratives, and sector-specific applications. This annotated guide provides professional librarian summaries and verified ISBN-13 numbers for 31 titles, noting publication details and any discrepancies from the original list.

---

## 1. The Digitalist Papers
**Erik Brynjolfsson et al. | Stanford Digital Economy Lab | September 2024**

Modeled on America's founding Federalist Papers, this ambitious policy essay series convenes leading experts from economics, law, technology, and political science to reimagine governance in the age of AI. Volume 1 explores how artificial intelligence intersects with democracy, offering a pluralistic, interdisciplinary roadmap for navigating transformative change. Co-chaired by Condoleezza Rice, Nathaniel Persily, and Alex Pentland, it represents a new model for public intellectual engagement with technological disruption.

**ISBN-13:** N/A (online policy series at digitalistpapers.com; not a traditional book)

---

## 2. Co-Intelligence: Living and Working with AI
**Ethan Mollick | Portfolio | April 2024**

An instant *New York Times* bestseller from Wharton's leading voice on AI, this guide offers the definitive practical playbook for working, learning, and living alongside generative AI. Mollick urges readers to engage with AI as co-worker, co-teacher, and coach, providing dozens of real-world examples while challenging us to harness AI's power without losing our human identity. Angela Duckworth calls it "the very best book I know about generative AI."

**ISBN-13:** 978-0593716717

---

## 3. The Emergent Mind: How Intelligence Arises in People and Machines
**Gaurav Suri and Jay McClelland | Basic Books | October 2025**

*Note: The original listing cited Karen Donovan and Ian McGilchrist as authors, which could not be verified. Research indicates the actual title is by Suri and McClelland.*

This paradigm-shifting work explores how human and artificial minds work through neural networks, asking fundamental questions about the nature of intelligence itself. With a Kirkus starred review and an endorsement from Robert Sapolsky, the book illuminates the surprising parallels between biological and digital cognition. Readers fascinated by the intersection of neuroscience and AI will find fresh insights into what makes minds emerge.

**ISBN-13:** 978-1541605282

---

## 4. The Worlds I See: Curiosity, Exploration, and Discovery at the Dawn of AI
**Fei-Fei Li | Flatiron Books | November 2023**

Named one of Barack Obama's recommended books on AI and a *Financial Times* Best Book of 2023, this moving memoir traces the improbable journey of a Chinese immigrant who became one of AI's most influential scientists. Dr. Li chronicles her creation of ImageNet, the dataset that catalyzed modern deep learning, while advocating powerfully for a human-centered, ethical approach to technological transformation. Geoffrey Hinton praises it as a story of "determination and grit."

**ISBN-13:** 978-1250897930

---

## 5. AI Ethics: A Textbook
**Paula Boddington | Springer | April 2024 (softcover)**

*Note: Author's first name is Paula, not Paolo.*

This comprehensive textbook bridges theory and practice to explore the critical ethical challenges of artificial intelligence. Boddington examines how AI forces us to address fundamental questions about human life, value, and meaning, covering topics from philosophical foundations to practical controversies in work, superintelligence, and moral machines. An essential resource for students and educators navigating AI's ethical landscape across 11 chapters and 522 pages.

**ISBN-13:** 978-9811993848 (softcover); 978-9811993817 (hardcover)

---

## 6. AI Snake Oil: What Artificial Intelligence Can Do, What It Can't, and How to Tell the Difference
**Arvind Narayanan and Sayash Kapoor | Princeton University Press | September 2024**

From two of TIME's 100 Most Influential People in AI comes an essential guide for separating AI hype from reality. Computer scientists Narayanan and Kapoor explain why much of "predictive AI" is snake oil, offering products that don't work and never will, while providing nuanced analysis of generative AI's genuine potential. This clear-eyed guide empowers readers to make informed decisions about AI in education, medicine, hiring, and criminal justice.

**ISBN-13:** 978-0691249131

---

## 7. The AI Con: How to Fight Big Tech's Hype and Create the Future We Want
**Emily M. Bender and Alex Hanna | Harper | May 2025**

*Note: Co-author is Alex Hanna (not Timnit Gebru); publisher is Harper (not MIT Press). Gebru wrote an endorsement.*

A sharp, accessible takedown of artificial intelligence hype by two of tech's most prominent AI critics. Known for their influential "Stochastic Parrots" paper, Bender and Hanna expose how tech corporations use AI narratives to justify data theft, surveillance capitalism, and labor devaluation. *Library Journal* calls it "a thorough, witty, and accessible argument against AI that meets the moment."

**ISBN-13:** 978-0063418561

---

## 8. Empire of AI: Dreams and Nightmares in Sam Altman's OpenAI
**Karen Hao | Penguin Press | May 2025**

An instant *New York Times* bestseller and National Book Critics Circle Award finalist from one of the few journalists ever granted inside access to OpenAI. Drawing on 300+ interviews and seven years of reporting, Hao delivers a deeply researched investigation into the company at the center of the AI revolution, including the never before told story of Sam Altman's firing and return. A global examination of AI's hidden human and environmental costs.

**ISBN-13:** 978-0593657508

---

## 9. AI Valley: Microsoft, Google, and the Trillion-Dollar Race to Cash In on Artificial Intelligence
**Gary Rivlin | Harper Business | March 2025**

Pulitzer Prize-winning investigative journalist Rivlin embeds with Silicon Valley's top AI players during the explosive post-ChatGPT era, following Reid Hoffman, Sam Altman, and Mustafa Suleyman as startups and tech giants collide. Weaving together the fascinating history of AI's evolution with real-time reporting on 2023 and 2024 breakthroughs and failures, this narrative account captures both the promise and peril of technologies reshaping how we live and work.

**ISBN-13:** 978-0063347496

---

## 10. AI Superpowers: China, Silicon Valley, and the New World Order
**Kai-Fu Lee | Houghton Mifflin Harcourt | September 2018**

A prescient and influential analysis of the US-China AI competition from one of the world's foremost AI pioneers with executive experience at Apple, Microsoft, and Google China. Lee argues China has caught up to America through its vast data resources, aggressive startup culture, and government support, while both nations must accept profound responsibilities. Beyond geopolitics, Lee provides a clear-eyed assessment of which jobs will be affected and offers a blueprint for human coexistence with AI.

**ISBN-13:** 978-1328546395 (hardcover); 978-0358105589 (paperback)

---

## 11. A Brief History of Intelligence: Evolution, AI, and the Five Breakthroughs That Made Our Brains
**Max Bennett | Mariner Books | October 2023**

A paradigm-shifting work bridging neuroscience and artificial intelligence that asks: why can AI beat grandmasters at chess but can't load a dishwasher? Bennett chronicles the billion-year evolutionary story of the brain through five key "breakthroughs," revealing where modern AI has matched or surpassed human capabilities and where critical gaps remain. Daniel Kahneman calls it "amazing," and Karl Friston deems it "an incredible resource."

**ISBN-13:** 978-0063286344

---

## 12. Why Machines Learn: The Elegant Math Behind Modern AI
**Anil Ananthaswamy | Dutton | July 2024**

Award-winning science writer Ananthaswamy demystifies the mathematical foundations powering today's AI revolution, from 17th-century calculus and linear algebra to modern deep learning architectures. This "Next Big Idea Club Must-Read" weaves together the colorful history of machine learning pioneers with accessible explanations of fundamental algorithms. Nobel laureate Geoffrey Hinton calls it "a masterpiece" that "presents the mathematics in the context of the social history."

**ISBN-13:** 978-0593185742 (hardcover); 978-0593185766 (paperback)

---

## 13. Teaching with AI: A Practical Guide to a New Era of Human Learning
**José Antonio Bowen and C. Edward Watson | Johns Hopkins University Press | April 2024**

This indispensable guide equips educators with research-backed strategies for harnessing AI as a powerful teaching tool while navigating critical issues of academic integrity, cheating, and the transformation of creativity and authorship. Bowen and Watson offer practical suggestions from interactive learning techniques to advanced assessment strategies, arguing that critical thinking and liberal arts education matter more than ever in the AI age.

**ISBN-13:** 978-1421449227

---

## 14. The Alignment Problem: Machine Learning and Human Values
**Brian Christian | W. W. Norton & Company | October 2020**

In this meticulously researched and "riveting" account, bestselling author Brian Christian explores the fundamental challenge of creating AI systems that do what we actually want, examining how algorithms inherit our biases and make consequential decisions about bail, mortgages, and employment. Finalist for the Los Angeles Times Book Prize, the *New York Times* declared: "If you're going to read one book on artificial intelligence, this is the one."

**ISBN-13:** 978-0393635829 (hardcover); 978-0393868333 (paperback)

---

## 15. Nexus: A Brief History of Information Networks from the Stone Age to AI
**Yuval Noah Harari | Random House | September 2024**

From the author of *Sapiens* comes this #1 *New York Times* bestseller that traces how information networks, from oral traditions and sacred texts to bureaucracies and AI, have shaped human societies and now threaten our very existence. Harari examines the complex relationship between information and truth, warning of urgent choices we face as "non-human intelligence threatens to annihilate us." *The Economist* calls it "strikingly original."

**ISBN-13:** 978-0593734223

---

## 16. The Cambridge Handbook of the Law, Ethics and Policy of Artificial Intelligence
**Nathalie A. Smuha (ed.) | Cambridge University Press | February 2025**

This comprehensive, interdisciplinary handbook provides essential reading for understanding AI's legal, ethical, and policy implications, with particular focus on European regulatory frameworks including the EU AI Act. Drawing on contributions from experts across law, philosophy, and technology, the volume covers AI applications in healthcare, finance, education, media, labor, and law enforcement. Available as Gold Open Access, making it an invaluable resource for scholars and policymakers.

**ISBN-13:** 978-1009367813 (hardcover); 978-1009367783 (ebook)

---

## 17. AI and the Legal Profession: Transforming the Future of Law (Second Edition)
**Francesca Ramadan (ed.) | Globe Law and Business | June 2025**

*Note: Editor may be listed as Francesca Ramadan rather than Francesca Tamamaha per publisher records.*

This comprehensive second edition serves as an essential guide for legal professionals navigating the rapidly evolving landscape of AI in law practice. Written by leading experts at the intersection of AI and law, the book explores how artificial intelligence is revolutionizing legal research, document review, and predictive analytics while addressing critical concerns about ethics, privacy, and algorithmic bias.

**ISBN-13:** 978-1837230884

---

## 18. The Singularity Is Nearer: When We Merge with AI
**Ray Kurzweil | Viking | June 2024**

In this long-awaited sequel to his influential 2005 work *The Singularity Is Near*, Google's legendary futurist presents an updated vision of humanity's technological future, reaffirming his predictions that AI will reach human-level intelligence by 2029 and that humans will merge with machines by 2045. Drawing on six decades of AI research, Kurzweil examines breakthroughs in nanotechnology, radical life extension, and brain-cloud connectivity. An instant *New York Times* bestseller.

**ISBN-13:** 978-0399562761

---

## 19. How To Think About AI: A Guide for the Perplexed
**Richard Susskind | Oxford University Press | March 2025**

Drawing on four decades of work in artificial intelligence, legal technology pioneer Richard Susskind offers a remarkably accessible and balanced guide that cuts through the confusion surrounding AI. Rather than providing answers, Susskind equips readers with the frameworks and vocabulary needed to think critically about AI's capabilities, limitations, risks, and regulatory challenges. Former Prime Minister Gordon Brown calls it "a must-read."

**ISBN-13:** 978-0198941927

---

## 20. The Optimist: Sam Altman, OpenAI, and the Race to Invent the Future
**Keach Hagey | W. W. Norton & Company | May 2025**

*Wall Street Journal* reporter Hagey delivers the first major biography of Sam Altman, the enigmatic leader driving the AI revolution as CEO of OpenAI. Based on more than 250 interviews, including extensive time with Altman himself, Hagey charts his rise from precocious childhood in St. Louis through Y Combinator to building OpenAI. The portrait that emerges is of a brilliant dealmaker who believes in technological progress with "almost religious conviction."

**ISBN-13:** 978-1324075967

---

## 21. The Thinking Machine: Jensen Huang, Nvidia, and the World's Most Coveted Microchip
**Stephen Witt | Viking | April 2025**

Through unprecedented access to Jensen Huang and Nvidia's inner circle, acclaimed journalist Witt tells the riveting story of how a video game chip company became the engine of the AI revolution and, in June 2024, the most valuable corporation on Earth. Winner of the FT and Schroders Business Book of the Year Award, this is essential reading for understanding the hardware foundations powering AI. Mustafa Suleyman calls it "gripping and brilliantly told."

**ISBN-13:** 978-0593832691

---

## 22. These Strange New Minds: How AI Learned to Talk and What It Means
**Christopher Summerfield | Viking | March 2025**

A neuroscientist and AI researcher with dual expertise offers readers the definitive guide to understanding Large Language Models like ChatGPT and Claude. Summerfield masterfully weaves together cognitive science, linguistics, and philosophy to explain how these "talking machines" work, whether they can truly think, and what their emergence means for humanity. Starred reviews from Publishers Weekly, Library Journal, and Booklist confirm it "rises to the top" in a crowded field.

**ISBN-13:** 978-0593831717

---

## 23. The Coming Wave: Technology, Power, and the Twenty-first Century's Greatest Dilemma
**Mustafa Suleyman with Michael Bhaskar | Crown | September 2023**

*Note: Originally published September 2023; paperback with new afterword released April 2025.*

From a co-founder of DeepMind and current CEO of Microsoft AI comes an urgent insider's warning about the dual-edged nature of transformative technologies. Suleyman argues that AI and synthetic biology will create unprecedented prosperity while threatening the very foundations of the nation-state. Bill Gates calls it "my favorite book on AI." A *New York Times* bestseller and finalist for the Financial Times Business Book of the Year.

**ISBN-13:** 978-0593593950 (hardcover); 978-0593593974 (paperback)

---

## 24. Atlas of AI: Power, Politics, and the Planetary Costs of Artificial Intelligence
**Kate Crawford | Yale University Press | April 2021 (paperback August 2022)**

A landmark critical examination that reveals AI as neither artificial nor particularly intelligent, but rather a technology of extraction, from lithium mines to underpaid data labelers to the surveillance apparatus. Drawing on a decade of fieldwork across warehouses, mines, and data centers, Crawford creates an indispensable map showing how AI concentrates power while depleting planetary resources and human labor. Named one of the "Five Best Books to Get Smart about AI" by the *Wall Street Journal*.

**ISBN-13:** 978-0300264630 (paperback); 978-0300209570 (hardcover)

**Salman Khan | Viking | May 2024**

The founder of Khan Academy provides the first comprehensive guide to the AI revolution in education, offering a hopeful yet realistic roadmap for teachers, parents, and students navigating this transformative moment. Rather than fearing ChatGPT, Khan shows how AI can personalize learning, adapt to individual student needs, and democratize access to world-class tutoring. Bill Gates calls it "a timely masterclass."

**ISBN-13:** 978-0593656952

## 26. Searches: Selfhood in the Digital Age
**Vauhini Vara | Pantheon | April 2025**

A genre-defying blend of memoir, journalism, and experimental writing that interrogates our complicated relationship with technology and AI through the lens of profound personal loss. Pulitzer Prize finalist Vara gained viral attention for asking a ChatGPT predecessor to help write about her sister's death; now she expands that experiment into a searching examination of how technology companies have both fulfilled and exploited our desire for connection. *The New Yorker* calls it "smart, funny, honest."

**ISBN-13:** 978-0593701522

---

## 27. Digitalization and Artificial Intelligence in Courts: Opportunities and Challenges
**Fernando Esteban de la Rosa, Pablo Cortés, and Nuria Marchal Escalona (eds.) | Oxford University Press | September 2025**

This authoritative edited volume examines how digitalization and artificial intelligence are transforming global justice systems, from online dispute resolution to the controversial concept of "AI judges." With contributions from international legal scholars and a foreword by Lord Briggs of the UK Supreme Court, the book provides rigorous analysis of algorithmic bias, data privacy, and cybersecurity challenges alongside comparative case studies from the EU, US, UK, and China.

**ISBN-13:** 978-0198918721

---

## 28. Shared Wisdom: Cultural Evolution in the Age of AI
**Alex Pentland | MIT Press | November 2025**

Renowned data scientist Alex Pentland argues that humanity's greatest breakthroughs, from the Enlightenment to the Scientific Revolution, emerged not from individual genius but from cultural inventions that accelerated collective wisdom. Drawing on his dual expertise in social science and technology, Pentland offers a compelling framework for ensuring AI amplifies rather than replaces human deliberation, presenting a hopeful vision for addressing global challenges.

**ISBN-13:** 978-0262050999

**Michael Hanegan and Chris Rosser | ALA Editions/Core | June 2025**

**Daron Acemoglu and Simon Johnson | PublicAffairs | May 2023 (paperback September 2024)**

*Note: Originally published May 2023; the September 2024 date corresponds to the paperback release.*

In this landmark work by two Nobel Prize-winning MIT economists, Acemoglu and Johnson deliver a sweeping thousand-year history demonstrating that technological progress doesn't automatically benefit everyone. **Martin De Saulles | Facet Publishing | June 2025**

At an About page and place it next to acknowledgments 

About This Exhibit
AI in the Library exists as both a physical display in the Robert Crown Law Library and this companion website. Fittingly, we used AI tools throughout its creation.
How We Made This
We used Canva for visual planning, NotebookLM for videos and infographics, and Claude, Gemini, and ChatGPT for drafting text. All AI-generated content was reviewed, fact-checked, and refined by library staff using traditional research methods.
This Site Is a Vibe Coding Example
This website demonstrates "vibe coding"—building software by describing what you want in plain language while an AI writes the code. We built it using Google AI Studio and host it through GitHub and Vercel. The site connects to three APIs: Google Gemini, Open Library, and Google Books.
Why We Share Our Process
Transparency matters. By showing how we used these tools—including their limitations—we hope to encourage informed experimentation within the Stanford Law community.

**Defining the About Page**

I'm currently focused on defining the "About" page component, specifically naming it `About.tsx`. I'll integrate this new component by adding a button next to the "Acknowledgments" button in the header, linking the former to the latter. The content itself is, thankfully, already available.


**Refining the About Page**

I'm now honing the "About" page content itself. I've broken it down into sections: an introduction explaining the project's dual physical and digital nature, followed by sections on our methodology and a "vibe coding" demonstration. I'm focusing on ensuring a smooth flow between the content sections, making it engaging and informative, as well as clear to visitors. The site-specific "Vibe Coding" section is where things are getting interesting.


**Detailing the Technicals**

I've been drilling into the technical aspects. The site's hosted via GitHub/Vercel and was built with Google AI Studio. It hooks into three APIs: Google Gemini, Open Library, and Google Books. I'm prioritizing the "Why We Share Our Process" section, emphasizing transparency to foster informed experimentation in the Stanford Law community. Now, I'm working to update `App.tsx` and the `Header` to implement the About button and page. I'm working to ensure it has a consistent visual style.


**Implementing the About Component**

I'm now implementing the `About` component in `About.tsx`. I've added a navigation button, styled consistently with the site, that calls the `onBack` function. The component uses a container with animation and styling. Within the container, a navigation element has a return button and heading. I'm focusing on ensuring it matches the site's overall aesthetic and user experience with consistent styling and interactive features.


**Describing the Intro**

I'm currently focused on the introduction for the "About" page. I'm starting with a concise statement about the project's dual physical and digital nature. This will be followed by a description of the AI tools we used for creation. I'll make sure it's clear and sets the stage. The text will emphasize the project's hybrid existence and the iterative nature of the process. I'm keen on establishing the integration of physical and digital aspects.


**Explaining the Vibe**

I'm now describing the "vibe coding" demonstration. I'm detailing how this website acts as a practical example. I'll highlight the use of Google AI Studio in the process and mention GitHub/Vercel hosting, plus the three APIs. I'm emphasizing that this showcases building software through plain language descriptions to drive AI code generation.


**Implementing the About Button**

I'm now integrating the "About" page into the main application flow. I'm focusing on updating `App.tsx` by importing the `About` component, adding state to manage the visibility of the "About" page, and resetting this state in the `handleBackToHome` function. I'm also adding the "About" button to the `Header` component. The `About` component will be rendered conditionally. I don't anticipate needing to touch other files. I'll focus on ensuring smooth navigation and a consistent user experience.
I have added the new "About" page and updated the application to include a navigation button for it in the header.

AI in the Library exists as both a physical display in the Robert Crown Law Library and this companion website. Fittingly, we used AI tools throughout its creation.

{/* How We Made This */}

How We Made This

We used Canva for visual planning, NotebookLM for videos and infographics, and Claude, Gemini, and ChatGPT for drafting text. All AI-generated content was reviewed, fact-checked, and refined by library staff using traditional research methods.

{/* Vibe Coding */}

This Site Is a Vibe Coding Example

This website demonstrates "vibe coding"—building software by describing what you want in plain language while an AI writes the code. We built it using Google AI Studio and host it through GitHub and Vercel. The site connects to three APIs: Google Gemini, Open Library, and Google Books.

{/* Why We Share */}

Why We Share Our Process

Transparency matters. By showing how we used these tools—including their limitations—we hope to encourage informed experimentation within the Stanford Law community.

Robert Crown Law Library Digital Exhibit • 2026

payload.text: The poster images on the main page are sort of dsitracting. Can we make clean cards so that it doesn't look cluttered here?

**Revising Category Card**

I'm focusing on the visual design of the `CategoryCard` components. I think the current images are distracting, so my goal is to produce "clean cards." I'm planning to redesign the `components/CategoryCard.tsx` file to get started. I need to simplify the presentation and reduce visual clutter.


**Refining Card Layout**

I'm experimenting with cleaner layouts for the `CategoryCard`. Currently, I'm leaning toward a split or top-image/bottom-text approach to avoid overly cluttered backgrounds. I'm also considering subtle backgrounds or using images as accents, to enhance the "clean" aesthetic. A dedicated image area and a dedicated text area is cleaner than text over image, and using that in the grid layout might work better.


**Designing Card Content**

I'm now thinking about the `CategoryCard`'s actual content separation from the image, to boost readability. I'm imagining rounded corners, a border and a shadow on hover for the container. Also, I'm considering using the cover image as a header instead of a full background. I'm also now thinking of a dark or light mode compatible solid background for the text.



**Structuring Card Details**

I've been working on a fixed-height layout for the category cards to maintain grid consistency. I am structuring the content as follows: image on top (40-50%) with potential overlay; a solid background content area below (50-60%), using white or dark gray depending on the theme. I'm moving away from text-over-image, and eliminating shadows, and leaning toward a clean border and hover effect. I am considering a slight image zoom on hover.


**Refining Typography & Sections**

I'm now focusing on the text hierarchy within the category card, aiming for clarity. I'm thinking of a structured approach: a small, uppercase, accent-colored section label, a large, serif title, and a lighter sans-serif description. A "Enter Gallery" link/icon will sit at the bottom, creating a clean separation. I'm revisiting the `constants.tsx` file to examine image formats.


**Defining Card Sections**

I've decided to stick with the "Image Top / Text Bottom" split, to maintain a clean aesthetic. The image will have a fixed height of `h-48`, with a hover scale effect, while the bottom section will contain the content. I'll utilize `h-full` to leverage the grid's height management, though I'll test `h-[22rem]` as an alternative.


**Adjusting Card Structure**

I am now focusing on the card's content area. I'm using `flex-1`, `p-6`, and `flex flex-col` for the details. The label will be smaller and subtle. The title is bolder, at `text-2xl`, with the description slightly smaller and limited to 3 lines. I'm using a primary-colored link with an arrow at the bottom. I'm also reviewing `App.tsx` and the grid layout, deciding between fixed or flexible heights for the cards in relation to grid uniformity. I'm considering using `h-auto`, `min-h-[something]`, or `h-[28rem]` instead of `h-80`.


**Finalizing Card Height**

I've decided to address the card's height directly within the component's structure. I'm focusing on ensuring grid row uniformity across different content lengths. I'm using `auto` with `flex flex-col h-full` on the card and ensuring that the parent `div` in `CategoryCard` has `h-full`. I am modifying `components/CategoryCard.tsx` to reflect this change.


**Implementing Image Handling**

I'm now implementing the image handling for each card. I'm ensuring it's full-width, with `object-cover`, and a slight zoom on hover. I'm adding a subtle darkened overlay to the image section, to define its edge. I'm aiming for a clean and subtle visual effect.


**Refining Card Interactions**

I'm now focusing on interactive feedback for the cards. I'm refining the hover effects, integrating subtle visual cues. I like the use of a slight zoom on hover and am further exploring the transition of colors to improve the user experience. I'm focusing on the accessibility of the hover effect as a primary focus.


**Analyzing Line-Clamp Plugin**

I'm verifying the `line-clamp-3` utility's compatibility with the CDN-included Tailwind version, assuming support for standard utilities. Considering the user's "distracting" image concerns, I'm now thinking about the impact of `object-cover` on potential poster text within the images. Although text cutoff could be odd, standardizing image areas helps keep readable text isolated on a clean background, which is the best approach without changing the images themselves. I will revisit the card height setup in CategoryCard.

To address the clutter caused by text-heavy poster images, I have redesigned the `CategoryCard` component. The new design separates the image from the text content, using a "split-card" layout. The image now occupies the top portion of the card, while the text sits on a clean, solid background below it. This ensures readability and creates a much cleaner, more uniform aesthetic for the main gallery grid.
